ascript.doc:
AScript compatibility layer for XScript.

Scripts written for AScript (`from ascript.android.xxx import ...`) run on XScript
unchanged for the supported surface: action, node, screen, system, ui, data, media.
Features that need AScript's proprietary services (HID hardware, NCNN models, the official cloud,
paid plugins) raise NotImplementedError with a clear message. YOLO, PaddleOCR and
cloud_control run on XScript's own engines (ONNX Runtime, the 云控 connection).

ascript._compat.doc: Shared helpers for the AScript compatibility modules.

ascript.android._websel_js.doc:
In-page half of WebSelector, injected into a WebWindow with evaluateJavascript.

The JS between the markers is also loaded verbatim by scripts/tests/websel.test.cjs
in headless Chrome, so keep it self-contained ES2017.

Hid.doc: AScript's ESP32 HID peripheral isn't available; falls back to normal gestures.

Ime.doc:
AScript action.Ime on XScript 输入法 (xscript.android.ime). When it is not the active IME, input falls back to
accessibility SET_TEXT / root, keys to key events, as before.

Path.doc: android.graphics.Path-like builder; curves are sampled into polylines.

addArc.detail: addArc(left, top, right, bottom, startAngle, sweepAngle)

addRoundRect.detail: addRoundRect(left, top, right, bottom, rx, ry, dir=0)

arcTo.detail: arcTo(left, top, right, bottom, startAngle, sweepAngle, forceMoveTo=False)

cubicTo.detail: cubicTo(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3)

rCubicTo.detail: rCubicTo(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3)

catch_click.doc: Show a full-screen overlay and return the Point the user taps (blocking).

gesture.doc: Run one or more Paths as a (multi-finger) gesture.

slide.detail: slide(x, y, x1, y1, dur=20, interpolator=None, control_points=None)
slide.doc:
Swipe with optional speed curve (android Interpolator) and Bezier control points.

control_points: flat list [cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2, ...] or an int (random control point count).

ascript.android.bluetooth.doc:
蓝牙: scan, classic serial (RFCOMM / SPP) and BLE GATT.

    from ascript.android import bluetooth
    bluetooth.enable()                                   # asks the user when bluetooth is off
    for d in bluetooth.scan(8):                          # classic discovery; scan(8, ble=True) for BLE advertisers
        print(d["name"], d["address"], d.get("rssi"))
    c = bluetooth.connect("00:11:22:33:44:55")           # SPP by default (HC-05, ESP32 BluetoothSerial)
    c.write(b"hello\n"); print(c.read(timeout=2))
    c.close()
    g = bluetooth.ble_connect("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF")
    g.write("6e400

BleConnection.doc: BLE GATT client. UUIDs may be full or short ("180d").

notify.doc:
Subscribe to notifications/indications; callback(data: bytes, char: str, service: str) runs on a worker thread.
callback=None unsubscribes.

Connection.doc: Classic RFCOMM socket (serial port profile by default).

read.doc: Up to `size` bytes, waiting at most `timeout` seconds for the first ones; b"" when nothing arrived.

ble_connect.doc: Connect to a BLE peripheral and discover its services (see .services).

connect.doc: Open a classic RFCOMM connection (SPP unless `uuid` is given). Pairing, if needed, is handled by the system.

enable.doc: True when bluetooth is on; otherwise shows the system "turn on bluetooth" dialog and returns False.

scan.doc: Scan for `timeout` seconds (classic discovery, or BLE advertisements with ble=True); returns devices with rssi.

ascript.android.cloud_control.doc:
AScript 云控 (`cloud_control`) on XScript's cloud connection (xscript.android.cloud).

    from ascript.android import cloud_control
    cloud_control.connect_to_ws("ws://192.168.31.90:3000")
    cloud_control.send({"gold": 180, "water": 200})
    cloud_control.close()

`connect_to_as` targets AScript's official server, which XScript cannot use; point
`connect_to_ws` at your own server (see docs/CLOUD.md and backend/xscript_server).

channel.doc: Same as system.channel(fun): fun(msg) for each server message.

KeyEvent.doc: Physical keys. Needs 无障碍. Fields: key_code, action ('down' / 'up').

NotificationEvent.doc: Notifications. Fields: package, title, text, time, raw (None), send().

TouchEvent.doc: View interactions seen by accessibility. Fields: action ('click' / 'long_click' / 'scroll'), x, y.

ascript.android.location.doc:
Android location compatibility API. Coordinates are WGS84.

Callbacks run on a daemon worker; keep the script alive while receiving updates.
Call close() to release subscriptions. mock.start/stop/status drive system-wide mock locations (developer option needed).

Location.doc: Snapshot of Android's Location with matching common getters.

MockLocationApi.doc:
System-wide mock location (AScript location.mock). The device must have XScript selected under
开发者选项 → 选择模拟位置信息应用 (granted automatically with root). Mocking ends with stop() or when the script ends.

close.doc: Stop receiving updates and remove Android listeners (safe to repeat).

gcj02_to_wgs84.doc: Iterative inverse (error well under 1 m inside China).

get_last.doc: Return the newest cached location, or None if Android has no cached fix.

request.doc: Subscribe to available GPS/network providers; replace the previous request.

ascript.android.media.doc: ascript.android.media: volume, vibrate, TTS, e-mail drafts, microphone recording.

recode.doc:
Record the microphone to `path` (.m4a/.aac/.mp4 = AAC, .amr/.3gp = AMR-NB, .ogg/.opus = Opus on Android 10+).

time: milliseconds. Given: block that long, stop, and return the file path (None when nothing was captured).
None: start in the background and return immediately; finish with stop_recode(). Needs RECORD_AUDIO (requested here).
Android only allows recording while XScript is visible; started from the background it may capture silence or fail.

send_email.doc:
Open the mail app with a pre-filled draft (the user taps send). `to`/`cc`: "a@x.com, b@y.com" or a list.

Returns True when a mail app (or the chooser) was opened; raises ValueError on an invalid address.

stop_recode.doc: Stop the current recording; returns the file path, or None when nothing was recording / no audio was captured.

ascript.android.node.doc:
ascript.android.node: Selector / Node with AScript semantics.

Differences from xscript.android.node:
- String constraints are regular expressions (full match), like AScript.
- find() / find_all() do not wait; find_all() returns None when empty.
- click()/long_click()/input()/slide() on a Selector are queued and run on found nodes.

on_event.doc:
Raw accessibility events (window changes, clicks, toasts, notifications...).

`listener(e)` gets an event with e.getEventType(), e.getPackageName(), e.getClassName()
and e.getText(), like AScript's AccessibilityEvent. Pass listener=None to stop.

WebNode.doc: One DOM element found by WebSelector: tag_name, bounds, text, value, attributes.

WebSelector.doc:
DOM selector for a shown WebWindow (AScript node.web.WebSelector).

    node = WebSelector(window).tag("a").text("/AScript/").find()
    WebSelector(window).attr("id", "user").input("tom").find()

Matches run in the page via WebView JavaScript. Strings match exactly;
"/regex/flags" is a JS regex. text() keeps the innermost matching elements.
Actions (click/long_click/input) are applied to the results of find/find_all.
Bounds are device pixels relative to the window's WebView.

ascript.android.plug.doc:
插件 (AScript `plug`).

AScript downloads plugins from its own server. XScript has no plugin server, but the
plugins scripts actually rely on for vision are built in, so the usual code runs unchanged:

    from ascript.android import plug
    plug.load("Yolov8Ncnn:1.3")      # also "yolov5", "yolov8", "yolov11", "Yolov11Ncnn", ...
    import Yolov8Ncnn as yolo
    yolo.load(R.res("best.onnx"), None, 5)    # ONNX instead of NCNN .param/.bin
    yolo.detect()

Other plugin names raise NotImplementedError. Third-party Python packages are installed
with `xscript.android.pip` instead. External Java c

JavaClass.doc: A class from a loaded plugin: new(), call_static(), get_static()/set_static().

JavaObject.doc: An instance: call(), get()/set(). `.java` is the raw Java object for APIs that take it.

load.doc: Register a built-in plugin module so `import <name>` works. Returns the module.

load_apk.doc:
Load an .apk/.jar/.dex/.zip with DexClassLoader. The file must be inside the app's own storage (projects, files,
cache); anything else raises ValueError. Returns a Plugin; the same file loaded twice shares one class loader.

load_apk_dir.doc: Load every plugin file in `directory` (non-recursive, sorted). Returns {file name: Plugin}.

ascript.android.screen on XScript: capture, colors, template matching, OCR.

`capture()` returns an android.graphics.Bitmap like AScript. Anywhere AScript accepts
`image=` / `bitmap=` / `source_img=`, a Bitmap, a BGR ndarray, a PIL image or a path works.

find_all.detail: find_all(text=None, rect=None, mode=None, binary=-1, confidence=0.1, image=None)

matrix.doc:
点阵字库: text recognised in ``rect`` with the font library file ``font_lib`` (e.g. ``R.res("font.t")``),
or None. ``region`` is the match similarity (0-1). The library is XScript's JSON format, built with
``MatrixFont`` (AScript's binary font.t cannot be read). Lines are read top to bottom, left to right.

matrix_detail.doc: Like ``matrix`` but returns ``{"text", "chars": [{text, rect, center_x, center_y, confidence}], "lines"}``.

mlkitocr_v2.detail: mlkitocr_v2(rect=None, pattern=None, confidence=0.5, bitmap=None, binary=-1, image=None)

paddleocr.detail: paddleocr(rect=None, pattern=None, confidence=0.5, max_side_len=1200, precision=16, bitmap=None, file=None, binary=-1, language='chinese', image=None)
paddleocr.doc: PP-OCRv5 on ONNX Runtime (models download on first use).

tess.detail: tess(data_file=Tess_CHI, rect=None, pattern=None, split_level=RIL_AUTO, white_list=None, black_list=None)

wait.detail: wait(text, timeout=10, rect=None, mode=None, binary=-1, confidence=0.1, image=None)

wait_click.detail: wait_click(text, timeout=10, rect=None, mode=None, binary=-1, confidence=0.1, image=None)

OcrX.doc: 点阵字库 as a GP task: ``Result.data`` is ``Ocr.matrix_detail``'s dict (or None).

find_all.doc: The recognised characters ([{text, rect, center_x, center_y, confidence}]) or None.

YoLov5.doc:
AScript `screen.YoLov5` on XScript's ONNX YOLO (v5 / v8 / v11 exports all work).

AScript ships NCNN models (.param/.bin); XScript runs ONNX. Export the same training run
with `yolo export model=best.pt format=onnx` and point `path` at the .onnx file (or a
folder holding one .onnx and, optionally, data.yaml / classes.txt for the names).

cache.doc: Freeze a frame so following searches reuse it. Call cache(False) to release.

ascript.android.screen.ascv.doc: Template-matching entry points compatible with AScript's screen.ascv.

find_all_sift.detail: find_all_sift(image_source, image_search, rect=None, threshold=0.5, rgb=False, maxcnt=0)

find_all_template.detail: find_all_template(image_source, image_search, rect=None, threshold=0.5, rgb=False, maxcnt=0, bgremove=False, ori=1, scale_range=None, fast=True)

ascript.android.screen.gp.doc:
Local GP pipelines reconstructed from the packaged task/UI interface.

JSON entries use ``id`` and ``data.params`` (Python argument literals), or
structured ``args``/``kwargs``. A package with a data.gp member is interpreted
declaratively (its Python is never executed). Legacy packages without data.gp
are AScript code exports (``as_gp_<name>/__init__.py`` defining ``gp(cv_img)``);
like AScript they are extracted and imported, unless ``allow_python=False``.

Project 图色插件: an id starting with "." (``.MyPlug``, ``.user.MyPlug``) names a
GPTask class in the running project, and must be declared in

run_json.doc:
Execute a JSON task array against an image (or the current screenshot).

Unknown tasks, executable expressions, cloud plugins and malformed
arguments raise an explicit error rather than yielding a partial result.

register_task.doc: Map a GP task id (e.g. a cloud plugin's ``module.Class``) to a local class.

run.doc:
Run a .gp: plain JSON, directory, or ZIP package.

data.gp (JSON) is preferred and never executes package code. Without it a
legacy Python export is imported and its ``gp(cv_img)`` called (AScript
behaviour); pass ``allow_python=False`` to refuse that.

ascript.android.screen.gp_tasks.doc: Common image-processing GP tasks (crop, gray, threshold, morphology, resize...).

Canny.doc:
Detect contours and return local-coordinate measurements in Result.data.

Offsets remain in Result.offset_x/y, as in the packaged interface. Resize
and rotation do not turn them into a screen-coordinate transformation.

CvFontLib.doc:
图片字库: recognise text by matching one small image per character.

``part_img[i]`` (a path or BGR ndarray) is the glyph for ``font_lib[i]``. Glyphs are matched in list
order and each match is blanked before the next glyph is searched, so put the larger or more
specific glyphs first. Matches are grouped into lines by the vertical centre (``spacing`` pixels)
and read left to right, lines top to bottom.

``Result.data`` is ``{"text": "12+3", "words": [[match, ...] per glyph], "group": ["12", "+3"]}`` or
``None`` when nothing matched. Match dicts are the usual template results plus ``"font"``; with

group_chars_by_distance.doc: Words split where the left edges of neighbouring glyphs are ``threshold`` or more apart (AScript helper).

recognize.detail: recognize(part_img, font_lib, confidence=0.95, rect=None, spacing=5, rgb=False, image=None)
recognize.doc: Convenience: run on ``image`` (path / ndarray / Bitmap) or a fresh screenshot; returns the text ("" if none).

sort_and_concatenate_chars.doc: Text of ``words`` in reading order, using 10px vertical buckets (AScript helper).

sort_group.doc: (text, glyphs in reading order, per-line strings).

ascript.android.screen.matrix.doc:
点阵字库 (dot-matrix font library) behind ``Ocr.matrix`` / ``Ocr.matrix_detail`` / ``OcrX``.

A font library is a small JSON text file, by convention ``res/font.t`` in the project::

    {"format": "xscript-matrix", "version": 1,
     "colors": ["FFFFFF-202020"],          # ink colour(s) "RRGGBB-DDDDDD" (colour - per-channel tolerance), or
     "threshold": 128, "invert": false,    # without colours: gray >= threshold is ink (invert: gray < threshold)
     "glyphs": [{"char": "1", "w": 5, "h": 7, "bits": "00100011000010000100001000010001110"}]}

Recognition binarises the area with the library's in

MatrixFont.doc: A dot-matrix font: one bitmap per character plus the rule that turns screen pixels into ink.

add.doc: Cut a glyph for ``char`` from ``image`` (path / ndarray / Bitmap; ``rect`` = [l, t, r, b]); trimmed to its ink.

binarize.doc: uint8 mask (1 = ink) of a BGR / gray ndarray.

recognize.doc: CvFontLib result data ({"text", "words", "group"}) on the binarised area, or None.

templates.doc: (BGR templates white-on-black with a 1px background border, chars), largest glyph first.

ascript.android.sensor.doc: AScript sensor decorators backed by bounded Android event queues.

ascript.android.shizuku.doc: Shizuku API mapped onto XScript's root shell / gestures.

ascript.android.sms.doc:
Read-only SMS compatibility API.

Rows match AScript: id, thread_id, address, body, date, date_sent, type,
read, subject, status. Dates are Unix milliseconds; read is boolean. Missing
numbers default to zero and missing or null strings to an empty string.

get_range.doc: Return inclusive 1-based range; invalid ranges yield an empty list.

query.doc:
Filter by address substring/type and order by date.

SQL LIKE wildcards in address retain their usual meaning. Nonpositive
limits mean all matching rows; negative offsets become zero. Missing
READ_SMS permission or a provider failure yields an empty list.

Config.doc: Run options of the current project (the switches on its screen in the app).

set_auto_run.doc: 开机自启: start this project after the device boots.

set_stop_re_run.doc: 停止后重新运行: re-run this project when it exits or crashes (not after a user stop).

send.doc: Report data to the 云控 server (same as cloud_control.send).

listen.doc:
call(event) for each notification (event.package / title / text / time / send()).

Needs 通知使用权 for full data; without it, accessibility notification events are used.
Pass call=None to stop.

get_card.doc: 卡密 of a packaged app's license (None when unlicensed or not packaged).

channel.doc:
fun(msg) for each 云控 server message (the connection is made in the app or with
cloud_control.connect_to_ws). Keep the script alive yourself (a loop).

reboot.doc: Restart the project in a fresh script process after `delay_time` ms (not a device reboot).

ascript.android.system.permission.doc: Runtime permission helpers (subset). Special grants open the matching settings page.

has.doc: Check the actual Android grant; undeclared/unknown keys return False.

request.doc: Runtime grants block for a result; Settings grants open a page and return DENIED.

ascript.android.vlm.asai.doc:
Natural-language vision with an explicitly selected compatible service.

No service is contacted until init() and an inference method are called. The
service must implement /vision/locate and /vision/ask; this is not an OpenAI
chat-completions adapter. Localization replies use uploaded-image pixels.

ask_value.detail: ask_value(question, value_type=str, rect=None, image=None, image_tokens=None, hint=None)

click.detail: click(target, timeout=0, rect=None, image=None, confidence=0.0, hint=None)

find.detail: find(target, rect=None, image=None, confidence=0.0, image_tokens=None, hint=None)

find_all.detail: find_all(target, rect=None, image=None, limit=10, confidence=0.0, image_tokens=None, hint=None)

init.doc:
Configure your service. ASCRIPT_AI_KEY/ASCRIPT_AI_BASE_URL are optional defaults.

Explicit init is always required. endpoint aliases base_url, including any
API prefix such as /v1. coord_space is sent to the service to interpret model
output; the service must normalize returned rects into uploaded-image pixels.

locate.doc: Convenience alias for find_all; returns mapped hit dictionaries.

wait.detail: wait(target, timeout=30, interval=0.0, rect=None, confidence=0.0, hint=None)

xscript.android.action.doc: Gestures, keys and text input. Coordinates are screen pixels.

Key.doc: System keys. `code(n)` sends a raw keyevent and needs root.

Touch.doc: Low-level touch stream: down → move* → up (one finger).

click.doc: Tap (x, y). `x` may also be a point-like object with .x/.y or a (x, y) tuple.

gesture.doc:
Multi-finger gesture.

strokes: list of {"points": [(x, y), ...], "start": ms, "duration": ms}.
Strokes run in parallel; each follows its points as a polyline.

input.doc: Set text on the focused (or first editable) field.

xscript.android.ai.doc:
Natural-language screen vision on any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint.

    from xscript.android import ai, screen
    ai.config(BASE_URL, model="qwen2.5-vl-7b")   # BASE_URL ends with /v1; key from XSCRIPT_AI_KEY
    hit = screen.ai_find("红色的关闭按钮")        # {"text", "rect", "center_x", "center_y", "confidence"} or None
    screen.ai_ask("当前是不是登录页？")           # plain text answer

Nothing is contacted until config() and a call. The key is never stored on
disk by this module; pass it in or set XSCRIPT_AI_KEY. Requests go to
{base_url}/chat/completions with one text part and one image_url data U

AiError.doc: Endpoint, protocol or configuration failure. status is the HTTP code or None.

ask.doc: Free-text answer about the screen (or rect / image).

config.detail: config(base_url=None, api_key=None, model=None, timeout=60, coords='pixel', image_tokens=1024, json_mode=False, headers=None)
config.doc:
Select the endpoint. base_url includes the API prefix, e.g. .../v1.

Defaults come from XSCRIPT_AI_BASE_URL / XSCRIPT_AI_KEY / XSCRIPT_AI_MODEL.
api_key may be empty for local servers that need none. json_mode adds
response_format={"type": "json_object"} to find requests.

find_all.doc: Every match as dicts like OCR results: text, rect, center_x, center_y, confidence.

wait.doc: Poll until found or timeout seconds pass; returns the hit or None.

xscript.android.cloud.doc:
云控 from scripts: report data, receive server messages, connect / disconnect.

    from xscript.android import cloud
    cloud.connect("wss://example.com/device?token=...", group="farm-1")
    cloud.send({"gold": 180, "water": 200})        # shown on the dashboard, per device

    @cloud.on_message
    def handle(msg):                               # server "message" frames / custom commands
        print("from server:", msg)

    cloud.status()   # {"state": "connected", "device_id": ..., "group": ..., "url": ...}

The connection belongs to the app (it keeps running between scripts and reconne

close.doc: Disconnect and forget the server URL.

connect.doc: Connect the app to a 云控 server (ws:// or wss://). The URL is saved for reconnects.

on_message.doc: Register `fn(data)` for server messages. Works as a decorator. Returns a token for off().

send.doc: Send a dict / list / str to the server (`{"type": "data"}` frame). False when offline.

wait_message.doc: Block until the next server message; returns its data or None on timeout.

Event.doc: One event. Fields are attributes (`e.text`) and keys (`e["text"]`); `e.type` is its kind.

send.doc: Notifications: open the notification (fire its contentIntent). Returns success.

dispatch.doc: Deliver one event dict to matching waiters and handlers (used by the pump and by tests).

loop.doc: Keep the script alive while handlers are registered (returns when all are removed, checked every `interval` seconds).

off.doc: Remove one handler (by token or function), all handlers of `event_type`, or everything.

on.doc:
Register `fn(event)` for `event_type` ("key", "touch", "notification", "toast", "a11y", "cloud", "float").

Keyword filters match event fields, e.g. `on("key", fn, key_code=24, action="down")`.
Returns a token for `off(token)`. Without `fn`, returns a decorator.

on_accessibility.doc:
@on_accessibility(): raw events (e.event_type, e.event_name, e.package, e.class, e.text).

`mask` is an AccessibilityEvent type mask; 0 = everything except WINDOW_CONTENT_CHANGED.

on_touch.doc: @on_touch("click"): view click / long_click / scroll with e.x, e.y (center of the view).

status.doc: {"types": [...], "attached": bool, "notification_listener": bool} from the main process.

wait.doc: Block until the next matching event and return it, or None after `timeout` seconds.

xscript.android.image.doc:
Image core shared by `xscript.android.screen` and `ascript.android.screen`.

Frames come from the device as raw RGBA (8-byte w/h header). numpy is required for
color and template work; OpenCV (cv2) for template matching. Both ship in the APK.

OcrResult.doc: One recognised line. Attribute access (AScript objects) and dict access both work.

Point.doc: Result point. Behaves like AScript's android.graphics.Point (x / y) and like a tuple.

bgr_to_raw.doc: BGR / BGRA / gray ndarray -> raw RGBA bytes with header.

capture_rgba.doc: Screen (or rect of it) as RGBA ndarray. None when capture is unavailable.

compare_colors.doc: True if the color points match at their absolute positions.

find_colors.detail: find_colors(colors, rect=None, sim=0.9, space=5, ori=2, max_num=0, image=None)
find_colors.doc: Multi-point color search. Returns Points of the first color point (screen coords).

find_templates.detail: find_templates(parts, rect=None, confidence=0.9, rgb=False, maxcnt=0, scale_range=None, image=None, ori=None, fast=True)
find_templates.doc:
parts: path or list of paths. Captures once and searches every template.

`ori=None` (XScript): best confidence first, `maxcnt` caps the combined list.
`ori=1..8` (AScript): `maxcnt` applies per template, results ordered by scan direction.

get_pixel.doc: (r, g, b) at screen/image (x, y) or None.

match_template.detail: match_template(source, part, rect=None, confidence=0.9, rgb=False, maxcnt=0, scale_range=None, index=0, offset=(0, 0), fast=True)
match_template.doc:
Template search on a BGR source. Returns AScript-shaped dicts in screen coordinates.

`rect` crops `source`; `offset` is added when `source` is already a screen sub-region.

ocr.doc: Run ML Kit OCR. Returns [OcrResult] in screen coordinates.

ocr_filter.doc: AScript semantics: keep lines where regex `pattern` matches; text becomes the joined matches.

raw_to_rgba.doc: Device raw frame -> HxWx4 uint8 RGBA ndarray (or None).

set_cache.doc: Freeze the current frame for all subsequent captures (AScript `screen.cache`).

sort_by_ori.doc: AScript scan-direction ordering (1..8) of template/OCR dicts by center.

to_bgr.doc: Accept None (capture), BGR ndarray, PIL image, Java Bitmap or file path -> BGR ndarray.

xscript.android.ime.doc:
XScript 输入法: type through XScript's own input method (an IME without a keyboard).

    from xscript.android import ime
    ime.switch()             # make it the current keyboard (silent with root; otherwise the system picker / settings)
    ime.commit("你好")        # insert at the cursor
    ime.delete(2); ime.clear(); ime.enter(); ime.key(67)
    ime.restore()            # back to the keyboard that was current before

Typing needs it to be the current IME with an input field focused (is_active()). action.input() uses it automatically
when it is active and falls back to accessibility / root in

enter.doc: The editor's action (search / send / go) when it has one, otherwise Enter.

restore.doc: Switch back to the IME that was current before switch(). True when switched back.

switch.doc: Make XScript 输入法 the current IME. Returns True when it is current now (False: user action needed).

xscript.android.location.doc: Android WGS84 location; shares the AScript subscription and cleanup state.

xscript.android.models.doc:
Model files for YOLO / PaddleOCR: where they live and how they get there.

    from xscript.android import models
    models.directory()                # model directory on the device
    models.paddle("v5")               # {"det": path, "rec": path, "cls": path}; downloads if missing
    models.fetch(url, "my/best.onnx", sha256="...")

Built-in PaddleOCR packs are the RapidOCR ONNX exports of PP-OCRv5 / v4 (mobile). Their
recognition models embed the character list, so no dictionary file is needed. Downloads go
to a temp file, are checked against the pinned SHA-256, then renamed into place.

directory.doc: Model directory: the app's external files dir on the device, ~/.xscript/models on a PC.

fetch.detail: fetch(url, name, sha256=None, mirrors=None, timeout=60, progress=None)
fetch.doc:
Download `url` (or each mirror + `url` if `mirrors` is given) to `directory()/name` unless present.

An existing file is kept when its checksum matches (or no checksum is given).

paddle.doc: PaddleOCR files for `version` ("v5" or "v4"): {"det", "rec", "cls"?} absolute paths.

xscript.android.node.doc:
Accessibility selector and node actions.

    from xscript.android import node
    n = node.Selector().text("搜索").find(timeout=5)
    if n:
        n.click()

String filters match exactly by default; call `.regex()` on the selector to treat them as
full-match regular expressions, or use `text_contains()`. Relations (`parent`, `child`,
`brother`) move the match set; filters after a relation apply to the new set.

find.doc: First match of `selector` inside this node's subtree.

brother.doc: No args: all siblings. brother(0.1) next, brother(-0.1) previous.

child.doc: No args: all direct children. child(1) first, child(-1) last, child(1.3) range.

filter.doc: Custom predicate on the raw node dict.

find_all.doc: Matching nodes; with `timeout`, re-query every `interval` seconds until something matches (one last look at the deadline).

parent.doc: No args: all ancestors. parent(1) direct parent, parent(2) grandparent, parent(1.3) range.

regex.doc: Treat string filters as full-match regular expressions (AScript semantics).

wait_gone.doc: True once nothing matches (checked every `interval` seconds), False if still there after `timeout` seconds.

dump.doc: Full tree payload as a dict: {"mode", "width", "height", "roots": [...]}.

xscript.android.onnx.doc:
ONNX model sessions (the inference engine behind `yolo` and PaddleOCR).

    from xscript.android import onnx
    s = onnx.Session("/sdcard/models/best.onnx")
    out = s.run(tensor)                 # {output_name: float32 ndarray}

On the device, inference runs in ONNX Runtime (Java) inside the script process; tensors
cross the Java/Python boundary as raw little-endian float32 bytes. On a PC the same class
uses the `onnxruntime` Python package when it is installed, so pipelines can be tested
against real models before they go to the phone.

Session.doc:
One loaded model. `threads` = CPU threads (0 = runtime default).

`accel`: "" (CPU, default) or "nnapi" (Android NNAPI; falls back to CPU if the device
rejects the model).

metadata.doc: Custom metadata of the model (Ultralytics stores names / imgsz / stride here).

run.doc:
Run with one float32 input. Returns {output_name: ndarray} in output order.

reduce="argmax": each float output becomes `<name>:idx` (int64) and `<name>:max`
(float32) over its last axis, computed next to the model. Use it for classifier
and CTC outputs with many classes; it avoids copying the full score tensor.

run_argmax.doc: (indices, max values) of the first output over its last axis.

available.doc: True when a backend can run models here (always on the device; PC needs onnxruntime).

load.doc: Cached Session per (path, threads, accel): loading a model costs far more than running it.

xscript.android.paddle.doc:
PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv5 / v4) text detection + recognition on ONNX.

    from xscript.android import paddle
    for line in paddle.ocr():                         # current screen
        print(line.text, line.confidence, line.rect)
    paddle.ocr_find("确定")                            # first line matching a regex

Models are downloaded on first use into the app's model directory (see
`xscript.android.models`), or pass your own files to `PaddleOcr(det=..., rec=..., keys=...)`.

Pipeline (same as PaddleOCR / RapidOCR):
  det: DBNet probability map → binarise → contours → min-area boxes → unclip
  cl

PaddleOcr.doc:
det / rec / cls: .onnx paths (cls optional). keys: dictionary .txt (optional when the
rec model embeds its `character` list, as the RapidOCR exports do).

classify.doc: Flip crops the orientation model calls 180° (with confidence > threshold).

ocr.doc: Text lines as [OcrResult] (same type ML Kit OCR returns), in screen coordinates.

crop_box.doc: Perspective-crop a text box; tall crops are rotated to horizontal.

ctc_decode.doc: [T, C] probabilities → (text, confidence). Index 0 is the CTC blank.

ctc_decode_argmax.doc: CTC greedy decode from per-step best class `idx` [T] and its probability `conf` [T].

detect_boxes.detail: detect_boxes(pred, src_h, src_w, thresh=0.3, box_thresh=0.6, unclip_ratio=1.5, max_candidates=1000, min_size=3, dilate=False)
detect_boxes.doc: DB post-processing: probability map [H, W] → list of 4x2 boxes in source pixels.

engine.doc: The default PaddleOcr, built from the managed models (downloaded on first use).

load_chars.doc: Character list: blank + keys file (or the model's `character` metadata) + space.

sort_boxes.doc: Reading order: top to bottom, left to right within a line (10 px tolerance).

xscript.android.permission.doc: Permission checks and user-facing Android grant requests.

xscript.android.pip.doc:
Install PyPI packages on the device at runtime (no APK rebuild).

    from xscript.android import pip
    pip.install("schedule", "pymysql==1.1.1")     # pure-Python wheels from PyPI
    pip.install("pandas")                          # Android builds from the Chaquopy index
    pip.install_requirements(R.root("requirements.txt"))
    pip.list()                                     # [{"name", "version", "location"}]
    pip.uninstall("schedule")

A project with a `requirements.txt` gets missing packages installed automatically before
`__init__.py` runs (only the first run needs the network).

W

Finder.doc: Collects installable wheels for a project from the Chaquopy index and PyPI (JSON API).

Target.doc: What wheels this device can use: Android API level, ABI, Python 3.10.

wheel_ok.doc: True if the wheel can be installed here. Returns (ok, native).

ensure_project.doc: Before a run: install the project's requirements.txt entries that are missing.

install.detail: install(*packages, index_url=None, upgrade=False, log=print, target=None, finder=None)
install.doc:
Install requirement strings ("name", "name==1.2", "name[extra]>=2"). Returns a summary dict.

Already-installed packages that satisfy the request are left alone unless upgrade=True.

installed.doc: {normalized name: (version, location)} of every importable distribution.

list.doc: Packages installed with pip.install (not the ones bundled in the app).

missing.doc: Requirement strings not satisfied by what is installed now.

parse_requirements.doc: requirements.txt lines → requirement strings (comments, blanks and pip options skipped).

resolve.detail: resolve(requirements, target=None, index_url=None, upgrade=False, finder=None, log=print, timeout=60)
resolve.doc: Pick and download wheels for `requirements` and their dependencies (depth-first).

xscript.android.screen.doc:
Screen capture, color and image search, OCR, AI vision.

from xscript.android import screen
screen.capture()                                  # PNG path on device
img = screen.capture_cv()                         # BGR ndarray
screen.find_colors("100,200,#FF0000|110,200,#FFFFFF", sim=0.9)
screen.find_image(R.img("ok.png"), confidence=0.85)
screen.ocr_find("确定")

ai_ask.doc: Ask a vision model a question about the screen; returns text.

ai_find.doc: Locate an element described in words via ai.config()'s endpoint; dict or None.

cache.doc: Freeze one frame for all following searches (faster multi-feature checks).

capture.doc: Save a PNG on the device. Returns the file path or None.

capture_cv.doc: BGR numpy array of the screen (or [l, t, r, b] region).

compare_colors.doc: True if all color points match at their positions. `colors` = 'x,y,#RRGGBB|...'.

detect.detail: detect(model, rect=None, conf=0.25, iou=0.45, image=None, classes=None)
detect.doc: YOLO detections on the screen: `model` is an .onnx path or a loaded `yolo.Yolo`.

find_all_colors.detail: find_all_colors(colors, rect=None, sim=0.9, space=5, ori=2, max_num=0, image=None)

find_all_images.detail: find_all_images(template, rect=None, confidence=0.9, rgb=False, maxcnt=0, scale_range=None, image=None)

find_colors.detail: find_colors(colors, rect=None, sim=0.9, space=5, ori=2, image=None)
find_colors.doc: First match of a multi-point color pattern → Point or None.

find_image.detail: find_image(template, rect=None, confidence=0.9, rgb=False, scale_range=None, image=None)
find_image.doc: Best template match → dict {center_x, center_y, rect, confidence, ...} or None.

ocr.doc:
All text lines → [OcrResult(text, rect, center_x, center_y, confidence)].

engine: None (the default from set_ocr_engine), "mlkit", "paddle" or "paddle_v4".
PaddleOCR loads its models on first use (about 1 s per full screen afterwards), reads
small Chinese text better and works on emulators where ML Kit cannot run.
confidence: drop lines below it. Default 0 for ML Kit, 0.5 for PaddleOCR (which
otherwise reports icons as low-confidence "text").

ocr_wait.doc: OCR every `interval` seconds until `pattern` shows up or `timeout` seconds pass (one last look at the deadline).

xscript.android.sensor.doc: Android sensor decorators; callback registrations are shared with ascript.android.sensor.

xscript.android.sms.doc: Read-only Android SMS API; shares the AScript compatibility implementation.

xscript.android.system.doc: Apps, device info, clipboard, key-value storage, shell and project resources.

Config.doc: Per-project run options, the same switches as the project screen in the app.

set_auto_run.doc: 开机自启: start this project after the device boots. Only one project can be the boot project.

set_stop_re_run.doc: 停止后重新运行: start the project again when it exits or crashes (not when a user stops it).

KeyValue.doc: Persistent key-value store shared across runs. Values are JSON-encoded.

R.doc: Paths inside the running project (res/, res/img/, res/ui/).

Schedule.doc: 定时任务. Times are device-local. One script runs at a time; see `if_running`.

clear.doc: Remove every schedule of `project` (default: the running project). Returns the count.

daily.doc: Run at "HH:mm" every day, or on `weekdays` (1 = Monday .. 7 = Sunday).

every.doc: Run every `minutes`, optionally only inside `window` ("08:00-23:00", may cross midnight).

list.doc: Schedules for `project` (default: the running project); pass project="*" for all.

once.doc: Run once at `at`: epoch seconds, a datetime, or "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm".

update.doc: Change fields of a schedule, e.g. update(id, enabled=False) or update(id, time="09:00").

open.doc: Launch an app by package name or label.

params.doc: Launch parameters of this run: the 云控 app_run "param" object ({} otherwise).

reboot.doc: End this run and start the project again in a fresh script process after `delay` seconds.

shell.doc: Run a shell command (via su when available and root=True).

status.doc: App status: channel, accessibility, root, capture source, resolution...

xscript.android.tree.doc:
Pure-Python query engine over the dumped UI tree.

The device dumps the tree as nested dicts (see NodeDumper.kt). This module indexes that
tree (parent links, sibling positions) and evaluates selector pipelines:

    stage filters -> relation (parent/child/brother) -> stage filters -> ...

Nothing here touches Java, so it runs in PC unit tests.

Indexed.doc: Wraps one dumped node with tree links. `raw` is the original dict.

Pipeline.doc: Ordered selector stages. Each stage is (relation, args, filters).

run.doc: Evaluate against dumped `roots`. `scope`: optional path whose subtree bounds stage 0.

collect_related.doc: Legacy one-hop relation (child = direct children, parent = direct parent).

match_node.doc: filters: dict {field: value} (legacy xscript form) or list of (field, op, value).

parse_xpath.doc:
Legacy step parser: //Type[@attr='v']/Child... -> list of (axis, type, attrs).

Kept for callers that inspect simple paths; evaluation goes through run_xpath, which
supports the full subset in xscript.android.xpath.

run_xpath.doc: Evaluate an XPath expression (see xscript.android.xpath for the supported subset).

xscript.android.ui.doc:
Overlay UI for scripts: toast, dialogs, HTML windows and a drawing canvas.

Dialogs and windows need the 悬浮窗 (overlay) permission.

Canvas.doc: Full-screen, touch-through overlay for drawing debug marks in screen coordinates.

arrow.detail: arrow(x1, y1, x2, y2, color='#ffaa00', stroke_width=2, duration=3000, id=None)

circle.detail: circle(x, y, radius, color='#00ff00', stroke_width=2, duration=3000, label=None, font_size=12, id=None)

cross.detail: cross(x, y, size=30, color='#ff0000', stroke_width=2, duration=3000, label=None, font_size=12, id=None)

line.detail: line(x1, y1, x2, y2, color='#65db79', stroke_width=1, duration=3000, id=None)

oval.detail: oval(x1, y1, x2, y2, color='#00ff00', stroke_width=2, duration=3000, id=None)

point.detail: point(x, y, color='#ff0000', radius=5, duration=3000, id=None)

polygon.detail: polygon(points, color='#00ffff', stroke_width=2, duration=3000, close=True, id=None)

rect.detail: rect(x1, y1, x2, y2, color='#ff00ff', stroke_width=2, duration=3000, label=None, font_size=12, id=None)

region.detail: region(x1, y1, x2, y2, color='#ff00ff', fill='rgba(255, 0, 255, 0.15)', stroke_width=1, duration=3000, label=None, font_size=12, id=None)

text.detail: text(x, y, text, color='#ffffff', font_size=14, duration=3000, id=None)

Window.doc:
HTML overlay window. JS talks back with `window.xscript.call(key, value)`
(alias `window.airscript.call`) and `window.xscript.close()`.

    win = Window("<button onclick=\"xscript.call('go','1')\">Go</button>", width="80vw", height="30vh")

    @win.on("go")
    def go(value):
        print("clicked", value)

    win.show(wait=True)   # blocks until closed

focusable.doc: Allow keyboard input into the page (steals focus from the app below).

js.doc: Evaluate JS in the page; returns the JSON-encoded result string (or None on timeout).

confirm.detail: confirm(msg, title=None, submit='确认', cancel='取消')

float_add_menu.doc:
Add a round button to the floating window's panel (AScript ``FloatWindow.add_menu``).

``icon`` is an image file path (``R.img(...)``); without a readable image the button shows the first
letters of ``menu_id``. ``callback`` runs on its own thread when the button is tapped, with no argument
(or with ``menu_id`` when it takes one). ``remove_system=True`` hides the built-in 运行/日志/打开/隐藏
buttons while custom ones exist. Adding the same ``menu_id`` again replaces the earlier button. The buttons
last until the script ends. The window itself still needs ``float_show()`` or the 悬浮窗显示 setting.

float_show.doc:
Show the floating window (悬浮窗) for this run, even while the app is on screen.

Same x / y / dim as AScript ``FloatWindow.show``: a positive number is a pixel position, a decimal
below 1 is a share of the screen (0.2 = 20%), -1 / 0 mean the far / near edge (right-bottom / left-top).
XScript always docks the window to the nearer side edge. ``None`` keeps the position the user dragged it to.
``dim`` is the opacity, 0-1.

prompt.detail: prompt(msg='请输入信息', title=None, value=None, hint=None, submit='确认', cancel='取消')

select.detail: select(items, msg='请选择', title=None, cancel='取消')

show_image.doc: Preview an image file in an overlay (tap to close).

xscript.android.xpath.doc:
XPath 1.0 subset over the dumped UI tree (uiautomator-style attribute names).

Supported:

- Paths: ``/``, ``//``, ``.``, ``..``, ``*``, ``node()``, and ``axis::test`` for child, descendant,
  descendant-or-self, parent, ancestor, ancestor-or-self, self, following-sibling and
  preceding-sibling. Name tests match the short class name (``TextView``) or the full one
  (``android.widget.TextView``).
- Predicates: ``[2]``, ``[last()]``, ``[last()-1]``, ``[position()<3]``, comparisons
  (``= != < <= > >=``), ``and`` / ``or`` / ``not()``, and nested paths used as existence
  tests (``//LinearLayout[

compile_xpath.doc: Parse `text` into an AST (cached). Raises XPathError on syntax errors.

select.doc: Evaluate `xpath` against dumped roots; returns tree.Indexed nodes in document order.

xscript.android.yolo.doc:
YOLO object detection (Ultralytics YOLOv5 / v8 / v11 and end-to-end exports) on ONNX.

    from xscript.android import yolo
    model = yolo.load(R.res("best.onnx"))          # class names come from the model metadata
    for d in model.detect(conf=0.5):               # current screen
        print(d.label, d.confidence, d.rect, d.center_x, d.center_y)

Train with Ultralytics on the dataset exported by the 标注工具, then export ONNX:

    yolo detect train data=data.yaml model=yolo11n.pt imgsz=640
    yolo export model=runs/detect/train/weights/best.pt format=onnx imgsz=640

Supported output layou

Detection.doc: One detected object. Attribute and dict access (`d.label`, `d["label"]`).

Yolo.doc:
A loaded detector.

names:  class names; default from the model metadata (Ultralytics exports carry them),
        or a list, a {id: name} dict, or a data.yaml path.
imgsz:  network input (h, w) or an int; default from the metadata / input shape / 640.

detect.detail: detect(image=None, rect=None, conf=0.25, iou=0.45, classes=None, max_det=300, agnostic=False)
detect.doc:
Detect on `image` (None = capture the screen; ndarray / Bitmap / PIL / path).

rect: [l, t, r, b] region; results stay in full-image coordinates.
classes: keep only these class ids or labels.
Returns [Detection] sorted by confidence.

decode.detail: decode(output, conf=0.25, iou=0.45, classes=None, max_det=300, nc=None, agnostic=False)
decode.doc: Raw model output → (boxes xyxy in network pixels, scores, class ids).

letterbox.doc: Resize keeping aspect ratio and pad to `size` (h, w). Returns (padded, scale, (pad_x, pad_y)).

load.doc: Load (and cache) a detector. `path` is an .onnx file.

nms.doc: Greedy NMS over [N, 4] xyxy boxes. Returns kept indices, best first.
